counterfactual_rationale: The record says DP attention changed the effective head count to 128 and selected a persistent MLA decode kernel that did not support that case, causing accuracy issues. A shape/dispatch test that includes this TP/DP head-count edge could plausibly have caught the bad backend choice before merge.

The failure is reported for DeepSeek R1 with CUTLASS MLA on B200 and manifests as an attention-constructor TypeError. Running the MLA serving path in CI on the affected B200/CUTLASS configuration could plausibly have exposed it.

The AITer backend rejected GQA shapes where num_kv_heads differs from num_heads even though the backend supports divisible grouped heads. Unit coverage over grouped-query head layouts on ROCm could plausibly have caught the over-broad guard.

The record is an ImportError caused by importing a ROCm/triton layout that exists for gfx950 but not upstream Triton on gfx1100. A ROCm hardware/compiler-version matrix import or smoke test could plausibly have failed before merge.

The fix is for Mixtral MoE under torch.compile, and the added coverage exercises the compiled MoE serving path rather than an isolated numeric kernel. A torch.compile model-level test could plausibly have caught this failure.
The PR describes a FA3 compile/import failure specific to cu118 and changes CMake/kernel packaging. A build matrix that included the CUDA 11.8 FA3 target could plausibly have caught it.

The discussion states full CUDA graph correctness broke when runtime batch size differed from capture batch size for FA3. A serving/graph-capture test varying capture and replay batch sizes could plausibly have exposed it.

The record says full KV locations were fed where SWA locations were required, causing CUDA illegal memory access under FA3 + EAGLE3 topk>1. A memcheck run on that hybrid-SWA speculative configuration could plausibly have flagged the bad access.

The crash occurs on the decode/CUDA-graph path when an empty recv_expert_num_tokens list produces non-None metadata that DeepEP combine cannot handle. A graph-enabled multi-node DeepEP serving startup/profile_run test could plausibly have reproduced the failure.

The root cause is an over-strict contiguous-query assertion for FlashInfer FP8 query quantization, while sliced QKV views have valid non-contiguous token strides. A tensor-layout edge test with split QKV views could plausibly have caught the assertion.

The linked issue reports a B200 GLM-5 FP8 accuracy drop from about 0.95 to 0.919 with FlashMLA sparse/kv kernels. A realistic model-accuracy workload on the affected B200 FlashMLA path could plausibly have exposed it, though the exact external kernel root is not shown.

The record is primarily a performance PR and only says it also fixes an int64 offset issue in triton_mrope, without showing a failure symptom or before/after correctness evidence. I could not tell from the record whether this was an actual kernel-correctness fix.

The PR explicitly fixes an illegal-memory-access bug for DSA with MTP that was introduced by another PR. Running the DSA+MTP path under a dynamic memory checker could plausibly have caught the bad access.

The crash happens on ROCm when an older AITer version lacks a sampling op, and the fix falls back to native sampling. A ROCm CI matrix that included the older AITer package could plausibly have caught the load-time failure.

The record says KV/prefill caching passed non-contiguous inputs to Marlin kernels that require contiguous memory, causing a crash. A kernel test that includes non-contiguous input tensors could plausibly have exposed this before merge.

The failure is a TPU RoPE initialization error caused by constructing buffers on a device path that XLA did not support. A TPU matrix smoke test for DeepSeek V2 RoPE initialization could plausibly have caught it.

The PR fixes MoERunner handling of quant config and gate selection, with discussion noting it fixed a gpt-oss H200 failure. A model-level MoE serving/evaluation path is the plausible pre-merge detector from the evidence.

The linked issue is a precision problem only for CUDA Graph + MTP + page_size=64, and the fix adds FA3 SWA spec handling for page sizes greater than one. Edge coverage over page-size and speculative-decode metadata could plausibly have exposed it.

The record is about enabling a faster CPU GDN implementation and float32 SSM cache gating on non-AMX CPUs, with correctness results presented as no-regression checks. I did not see evidence of wrong output, crash, or severe availability failure caused by a kernel bug.

The PR describes an intra-CTA data race where a load can run before another warp commits its store, producing garbage offsets and sporadic illegal addresses. A warp/barrier race analysis could plausibly have flagged the store-load-without-barrier pattern.

The fix gates gfx950-only FP4 operations so MI300X/gfx942 does not execute unsupported instructions. Running the FP4 enablement path on MI300X in hardware-matrix CI could plausibly have caught the illegal-instruction crash.

The Hunyuan production video shape overflows int32 row-offset arithmetic and causes illegal memory access. A large-shape indexing test near the INT32_MAX boundary could plausibly have exposed the bug.

The record ties the failure to hd256 FP8 prefill on gfx950 where 0-D descale tensors prevented selecting the supported ASM kernel. Unit tests over descale ranks and head_dim=256 on gfx950 could plausibly have caught this.

The bug is a FlashInfer ragged prefill plan that reads unwritten cache slots instead of cached prefix lengths, producing a large numerical error. A deterministic backend test that poisons unwritten extend slots, like the added regression, could plausibly have caught it.
The PR says the fusion code broke VL models and validates with Hopper E2E VL model tests. The evidence points to model-level compile/fusion coverage as the plausible detector.

The discussion shows EAGLE accuracy failing when CUDA graph is disabled and then passing after the fix. A speculative-decoding serving/evaluation test with --disable-cuda-graph could plausibly have exposed it.

The root cause is deterministic RNG causing FlashInfer MNNVL socket name collisions under concurrent jobs, leading to inconsistent collective state and crashes. A repeated/concurrent multi-job test with identical seeds could plausibly have exposed the collision.
The record says the fix addresses an nvcc internal compilation error in the custom all-reduce/JIT-kernel path. A compiler/build matrix covering that nvcc configuration could plausibly have caught it.

The stated motivation is a checkpoint weight-loading bug when expert gate and up_proj weights are not fused, plus a library-reference update. That root appears to be model/checkpoint integration rather than a kernel-correctness failure.
The PR says tensor parallel on XPU broke after upgrading to Torch 2.5 and fixes it by introducing an XPU communicator. An XPU + Torch 2.5 matrix test could plausibly have caught the breakage.
